text.p: Bonds closed down as Bunds softened and the local market was expected to continue to take its lead from Germany on Wednesday, providing the Italian market did not come under heavy pressure, traders said.
"The market was illiquid and eased at the close after Bunds came off their highs and to some, limited extent with the steepening of the losses in the (Italian) BTP," said one trader.
Traders said that the longer end was showing good support at around 115 basis points above the German Bund.
"The present spread (in the 10 -year) against Germany is only going to widen if Italy drags down the peripheries," said another trader.
Futures traders saw the contract moving in a range of 108.25-108.75 on Wednesday.
The money market was seen continuing stable.

But the escudo, which benefitted from commercial buying on Tuesday, could correct on Wednesday unless fresh commercial interest emerges as both the Spanish peseta and the Italian lira remain under pressure, traders said.
